sentences.text: Ngwevu is a massospondylid sauropodomorph dinosaur known from a single fossil specimen cataloged as BP/1/4779. This animal lived in the Lower Jurassic of South Africa and is distinguished by a unique set of sixteen traits, including a ridge on the backside of the jugal bone.

The only known specimen was discovered in 1978 by James William Kitching on Tevrede Farm in the Fouriesburg district. It was originally thought to be a specimen of Massospondylus but was reclassified as a new genus and species in 2019.
Histological studies indicate the Ngwevu holotype was an adult approximately ten years old when it fossilized, ruling out the hypothesis that it was a juvenile.

The wider snout of Ngwevu suggests it had a more generalist diet compared to the more selective Massospondylus carinatus. Ngwevu likely had a stronger bite than Massospondylus carinatus due to its robust jaw and skull features, suggesting they occupied different ecological niches.
Phylogenetic analysis places Ngwevu within the family Massospondylidae.

Ngwevu fossils are found in the Clarens Formation, dating to the Pliensbachian to early Toarcian stages. The animal lived between 201.4 and 192.9 million years ago, spanning the Hettangian to Sinemurian stages.
Some paleontologists hypothesized that Ngwevu might be a younger, less developed specimen of Massospondylus, though this was later rejected.
